title: What are the three ways to set a price, and when do you use each?
description: Ways to set a price once you know the floor and the ceiling.
hook: There are three common ways to set a price, and each one answers a different question. Knowing all three helps you sound balanced in a pricing case. Here they are.
body:
When it helps

Ways to set a price once you know the floor and the ceiling.

The checklist

Cost-plus

  • Unit cost × (1 + target markup)

Competitor-based

  • Match, undercut or charge a premium

Value-based

  • Share of the value the customer gets

Launch strategy

  • Skim: start high
  • Penetrate: start low

An example

A start-up makes software that saves accountants five hours a month. Cost-plus says: our cost is £8 a user, add 50%, charge £12. Competitor-based says: rivals charge £20 to £30. Value-based says: five hours of an accountant's time is worth around £150, so even £40 is a bargain. The three methods give very different numbers, which is exactly why a good answer looks at all three.

How it sounds in an interview

I'd look at the price from three sides: what it costs us, what rivals charge, and what it is worth to the customer. The answer usually sits between the cost floor and the value ceiling.
outro: The Pricing methods checklist is also on the free frameworks page. Next in this topic: Should a client build, partner or buy to get into a new market?
